Store RR only when flag bit 4 is set and the values are not synthesized, and call HRV 'exploratory, needs validation'. Heart-rate anomalies, including the signal dropping out, only pull the next check-in forward. They never escalate.

findings.topic: Using the watch's own haptics as the discreet 'are you OK?' buzz
findings.detail: Apple: 'If your iPhone is locked or asleep, you'll receive notifications on your Apple Watch, unless your Apple Watch is locked.' Notifications appear on one device, not both, and if the devices disconnect they go to the iPhone. On iOS 16.4+, Web Push works for Home Screen web apps whose manifest display is standalone or fullscreen, after a user gesture. Those notifications also show on a paired Apple Watch, and no Apple Developer account is needed (https://webkit.org/blog/13878/web-push-for-web-apps-on-ios-and-ipados/).
findings.recommendation: The team has no vibration motor, so send the PROMPTED and REMINDED nudges as a Telegram message from the bot to the wearer's own account (or Web Push to the wearer's installed PWA). With the iPhone locked, the Apple Watch taps the wrist. Keep the text neutral ('Tap twice if all good'), and keep the scrunchie LED blink as the primary cue.

findings.topic: Hosting tonight without a credit card
findings.detail: A Cloudflare quick tunnel (`cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000`) needs no account. It gives a random trycloudflare.com hostname that changes when the process restarts, has no uptime guarantee, allows 200 in-flight requests (429 beyond that) and does not support SSE. WebSockets do work through quick tunnels (https://stackharbor.com/en/knowledge-base/cf-quick-tunnel-trycloudflare-guide/). ngrok free shows an interstitial in front of all HTML browser traffic, which would hit the judge's QR page, and allows 20,000 HTTP requests/month and 1 GB out (https://ngrok.com/docs/pricing-limits/free-plan-limits). Render free sleeps after 15 minutes without inbound traffic and takes about a minute to wake. Background workers are not free and free Postgres expires after 30 days (https://render.com/docs/free). Railway's trial is a one-time $5 for up to 30 days, with 1 GB RAM. Its 'Limited Trial' restricts outbound network access until GitHub-based verification (https://docs.railway.com/pricing/free-trial). Fly.io's trial is 2 machine-hours or 7 days, trial machines auto-stop after 5 minutes, and a card is needed after that (https://docs.fly.io/about/free-trial). Vultr requires a card or PayPal, and users report a $5 deposit (https://lowendtalk.com/discussion/184879/vultr-new-free-plan/p1).
findings.recommendation: Run uvicorn on the laptop with a Cloudflare quick tunnel, plus Tiger Cloud for state. Run cloudflared as its own long-lived process so that kill -9 on uvicorn keeps the URL (the tunnel returns 502 until the server is back). Generate QR codes and device config from a PUBLIC_BASE_URL env var at runtime. Rule out ngrok free: a 5 s heartbeat plus 1 s page polling burns the 20k monthly requests within hours, and the interstitial breaks the judge's QR page. Do not use Vultr, Fly or Render for the live demo. Optional: a named Cloudflare tunnel gives a stable hostname if a teammate already has a domain on Cloudflare.

findings.topic: Contact alerts: SMS vs Web Push vs a foreground page
findings.detail: A Twilio trial needs no credit card (https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/trials). It can message only verified numbers (up to 5), only within the sign-up country, and only with Twilio templates. A toll-free number must be verified before sending to the US or Canada (https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/guides/how-to-use-your-free-trial-account). Chrome's autoplay rules: muted autoplay is always allowed, but sound needs a prior user interaction with the domain. An AudioContext created before a gesture starts 'suspended' and needs resume() after a gesture (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/autoplay). navigator.vibrate does not vibrate on iOS Safari (https://bugnet.io/blog/fix-web-game-vibrate-api-not-available-ios-safari). The Screen Wake Lock API is in Safari from 16.4, is released when the page is hidden, and has a reported bug in Home Screen apps (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/wake-lock, https://webkit.org/b/254545). TOPOLOGY
- The ESP32 scrunchie joins the iPhone hotspot (Maximize Compatibility ON) and sends HTTPS POSTs to https://<random>.trycloudflare.com. cloudflared runs as a long-lived process on the demo laptop and forwards to FastAPI (uvicorn :8000) on the same laptop. - Core rule, enforced in code: sensor and heart-rate anomalies can only create a PULL_FORWARD timer that moves ARMED to PROMPTED. Only timer expiry, which means no human response, can move a session to ESCALATED_*.

STATE MACHINE
Store this in sessions.state with sessions.version, which is incremented on every transition. Every transition runs `UPDATE sessions SET state=$to, version=version+1 WHERE id=$id AND version=$v AND state = ANY($allowed_from)`. If zero rows change, the request is a duplicate or stale and is ignored.

Transitions:
- ARMED -> PROMPTED: triggered by a CHECKIN_DUE timer or a sensor pull-forward. Command: LED pulse plus a Telegram nudge to the wearer's own phone, which taps the Apple Watch. Deadline T1: 20 s in the demo, 2 min in real use.
- PROMPTED -> ARMED: on a double squeeze (OK). Schedules the next CHECKIN_DUE.
- PROMPTED -> REMINDED: on T1 expiry. The server picks challenge_n from 1-3, the device blinks n times, and the wearer must squeeze n times. Deadline T2: 20 s in the demo. A wrong count gets one retry.
- REMINDED -> ARMED: on the correct challenge reply.
- REMINDED -> ESCALATED_L1: on T2 expiry. Opens an alert of kind NO_RESPONSE, sends outbox messages to the priority-1 contact, and creates location_share (expires_at = now() + 60 min). Ack deadline T3: 45 s in the demo.
- ESCALATED_L1 -> ESCALATED_L2: on T3 expiry. Notifies contact #2 (the judge's QR page) and re-pings contact #1. After that it re-notifies every 60 s with a cap. It never calls emergency services; the UI shows '911 call (SIMULATED - not placed)'.
- ESCALATED_L1/L2 -> RESOLVED: on the first ack from any contact. The other contacts are told '<name> is handling it'. The location share stays live until the user or the acknowledging contact closes it, or until it expires.
- PROMPTED, REMINDED or ESCALATED_* -> FALSE_ALARM: when the wearer enters the real PIN or does the OK pattern after escalation. Already-notified contacts get a 'False alarm - cancelled by Maya with PIN at 21:17' follow-up.
- Any active state -> DURESS_SILENT: on the duress squeeze pattern or duress PIN. The device and app get a response byte-identical to a real cancel (same status, body and timing). Server-side, the session immediately opens an alert of kind DURESS to contact #1 with a short ack deadline, then follows the L1 -> L2 path. It never sends anything visible back to the device.

LOST_CONTACT
- Track this in a second column, sessions.link_state (OK or LOST_CONTACT), so a lost link never pauses a pending countdown. This is KAZE's 'server-side countdown continues if the phone disconnects'.
- The ESP32 heartbeat every 5 s sets devices.lease_expires_at = now() + 20 s. A LEASE_CHECK timer, or a worker query like `WHERE lease_expires_at < now() AND link_state='OK'`, flips link_state and opens a LOST_CONTACT alert. Its wording is distinct and lower urgency: "StillHere lost contact with Maya's device (battery or signal?). This is NOT a missed check-in."
- If a PROMPTED or REMINDED deadline is pending, it keeps running and escalates as NO_RESPONSE.
- When the heartbeat returns: link_state = OK, plus a 'contact restored' message.

TIMER WORKER (every 1 s, safe with N workers)
BEGIN;
SELECT id, session_id, kind, expected_version FROM timers WHERE fired_at IS NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL AND fire_at <= now() ORDER BY fire_at LIMIT 20 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;
Then for each timer: SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id = $s FOR UPDATE. If the version does not match, set the timer's outcome to 'stale'. Otherwise do the guarded UPDATE of sessions, INSERT the next timer, INSERT outbox rows with ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING, and INSERT the audit_log row.
UPDATE timers SET fired_at = now() ...;
COMMIT;
- A kill -9 anywhere before COMMIT rolls the whole transition back, and the next process redoes it from the persisted deadline.
- Side effects go through the outbox. The sender claims rows with `UPDATE outbox SET status='sending', locked_until=now()+'30 s' WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... WHERE status='pending' AND next_attempt_at <= now() FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 10) RETURNING *`, calls Telegram, and then marks the row 'sent' with the message_id. A reaper resets 'sending' rows whose locked_until has passed.
- Delivery is therefore at-least-once: a crash between the send and the mark could cause a duplicate. Say so to the judges as the deliberate safety trade-off.
- On a 429, set next_attempt_at = now() + retry_after.

## 1. Product summary and 30-second pitch

**StillHere** is a scrunchie that works as a safety check-in device. You wear it on the wrist, or in your hair when you have no pockets and no free hands.

**How it works:**
- **Check-ins.** Squeeze twice and it means "I'm OK." Squeeze-squeeze-hold also looks like "OK" on the device, but it silently asks your contacts for help.
- **Motion and heart rate only bring the next check-in forward.** An accelerometer in the scrunchie looks for falls, head drops and unusual sway. Your own Apple Watch (or a Fitbit Charge 6) supplies heart rate. None of these signals ever decides you are in trouble. An anomaly only makes StillHere ask "are you OK?" sooner, with a scrunchie blink plus a tap on your own watch.
- **Escalation happens only when you don't answer.** A countdown on the server keeps running even if your phone dies or our server crashes. It notifies your trusted contacts in order until a person taps "I'm on it."
- **Lost contact is a separate alert.** If the device stops reporting, contacts get a different, lower-urgency message.
- **Privacy.** Contacts see nothing until an alert. Location is shared only at alert time and the link expires.
- **Incident log.** Every event goes into a timestamped, tamper-evident log that the user owns. It can help someone who cannot remember the night report it and ask for testing quickly. GHB is not on routine toxicology screens ([Swiss Med Wkly](https://smw.ch/index.php/smw/article/download/409/406/806)).

**30-second pitch.** Galit delivers it, aimed at bank and big-tech engineers:

> "Canada doesn't even count drink spiking. Statistics Canada files it under 'other assaults' ([Global News](https://globalnews.ca/news/4367269/n-s-police-to-review-drink-tampering/amp)). The dangerous window is the gap between the moment you can't ask for help and the moment anyone notices. In spy movies they hide weapons in their hair. We hide help in yours. Squeeze twice: you're fine. Squeeze-squeeze-hold: it looks exactly the same, but your people are being called. Your watch and our motion sensor never decide you're in trouble. They only make StillHere ask sooner. If you don't answer, a countdown stored in Postgres escalates through your contacts until a human says 'I'm on it'. It survives your phone dying, and it survives us killing the server live. Judge, scan this: you're Contact #2. Keep your phone out."

Points that engineers will notice:
- Timers are rows in the database, claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
- Side effects go through a transactional outbox.
- Device events are idempotent.
- The audit log is append-only and hash-chained.
- We run a live `kill -9` mid-countdown.

**Data flow:**
1. **Device to server.** The scrunchie samples at 100 Hz and computes features and events on the device. It sends `POST /v1/device/heartbeat` every 5 s, which renews its lease and carries up to five 1 Hz feature rows. It sends `POST /v1/device/events` immediately for `squeeze_ok`, `squeeze_duress`, `challenge_reply`, `fall`, `head_drop` and `sway_anomaly`. The heartbeat reply carries the downlink: `{led, blink_n, nudge}`. There is no inbound socket, broker or MQTT.
2. **Heart rate to server.** The watch's heart rate reaches HeartCast on the iPhone. The iPhone re-advertises it as a standard BLE Heart Rate sensor. The laptop's Chrome `/hr-bridge` page subscribes to it and calls `POST /v1/hr` once a second.
3. **Rules.** FastAPI stores samples in hypertables. A rule compares signals with the wearer's own baseline. **Its only possible output is a `PULL_FORWARD` timer (ARMED → PROMPTED).** Only a deadline expiring with no human response can move a session to `ESCALATED_*`.
4. **Side effects.** Transitions write outbox rows. `outbox_sender` delivers them to Telegram (contacts, and the wearer's own nudge). The `/c/<token>` page polls `/v1/contact/<token>/status` every second.
5. **Acknowledgement.** A Telegram callback or a web Acknowledge resolves the alert. The other contacts get "<name> is handling it."

**Why this topology:**
- Quick tunnels need no account. WebSockets work through them; SSE does not ([Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/), [StackHarbor](https://stackharbor.com/en/knowledge-base/cf-quick-tunnel-trycloudflare-guide/)).
- ngrok's free tier adds an interstitial page and a 20k requests/month cap ([ngrok](https://ngrok.com/docs/pricing-limits/free-plan-limits)), so it is ruled out.
- Telegram long polling (`getUpdates`) needs no public URL ([Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api)).
- The ESP32 talks to the public tunnel URL, not to the laptop's hotspot IP, because iPhone Personal Hotspot does not guarantee client-to-client traffic ([Apple DTS](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/79141)).

## 5. Firmware modules (Arduino-ESP32 core 3.x)

**Runtime:**
- `task_sense` on core 1 polls the FIFO every 100 ms and the FSRs every 10 ms.
- `task_net` on core 0 handles heartbeat, events and retries.
- A FreeRTOS queue connects them.
- Libraries: `Adafruit_ADXL345_Unified` (`begin(0x53)`, `setRange(ADXL345_RANGE_16_G)`, `setDataRate(ADXL345_DATARATE_100_HZ)`, `writeRegister`/`readRegister`), `ArduinoJson`, `HTTPClient` plus `NetworkClientSecure`, `Preferences` (NVS), and `mbedtls/md.h` for HMAC.

**Every detector calls one function only:**

```
request_early_checkin(reason, severity, features)
```

It shows the LED, posts the event, and the server pulls the next check-in forward. **No firmware path contacts anyone.**

### 5.1 ADXL345 setup

Settings follow AN-1023 ([ADI](https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/application-notes/AN-1023.pdf), [mirror](https://www.all-electronics.de/files/2025/10/15/522ag1010.pdf)) and the datasheet ([SparkFun](https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/9/1/8/9/9/ADXL345.pdf)).

```
0x2D=0x00  standby      0x2E=0x00  ints off     0x31=0x0B  FULL_RES ±16 g (3.9 mg/LSB)
0x2C=0x0A  100 Hz       0x28=0x0C  THRESH_FF 0.75 g     0x29=0x06  TIME_FF 30 ms
0x24=0x30  THRESH_ACT 3 g (dc)    0x25=0x03  THRESH_INACT 0.1875 g   0x26=0x02  TIME_INACT 2 s
0x27=0x7F  act dc / inact ac, all axes   0x2F=0x00  INT_MAP   0x38=0x90  FIFO stream, watermark 16
0x2E=0x1C  enable activity/inactivity/free-fall   0x2D=0x08  measure
```

**Reading:**
- Every 100 ms: `n = read(0x39) & 0x3F`, then do `n` **6-byte burst reads from 0x32**. Single-byte reads lose FIFO data ([datasheet](https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/9/1/8/9/9/ADXL345.pdf)), and Adafruit's `getEvent()` reads each axis separately ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adafruit/Adafruit_ADXL345/master/Adafruit_ADXL345_U.cpp)).
- `int_bits |= read(0x30)` once per loop, because reading INT_SOURCE clears it.
- Calibrate 5 s still at boot and subtract the per-axis offset. Typical offset is ±40 mg on x/y and ±80 mg on z.
- Wi-Fi must never block sensing for more than about 250 ms, because the 32-sample FIFO fills in 320 ms.

### 5.2 Squeeze decoder (FSR)

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Sampling | 100 Hz, EMA α = 0.3 |
| Signal | max over both FSRs of (mV − baseline) |
| Baseline | Slow EMA (τ ≈ 10 s), updated only while idle. It absorbs the elastic's pre-load |
| Thresholds | Calibrate with 3 firm squeezes to get `vmax`. ON = base + max(300 mV, 0.40·(vmax − base)); OFF = base + max(150 mV, 0.20·(vmax − base)) |
| Debounce | 3 consecutive samples (30 ms) on each edge |
| Press classes | under 80 ms ignored; 80–1000 ms SHORT; 1000–5000 ms LONG; over 5000 ms PRESSURE_ARTIFACT (logged, re-baseline, **never** duress) |
| End of sequence | 1000 ms with no new press (configurable 600–2000 ms) |
| Decode | `[S,S]` → OK. Two or more presses with the last LONG and the rest SHORT → **DURESS**. Five or more SHORT within 3 s → overt HELP (optional). Anything else → UNRECOGNIZED, which counts as no response and gets one re-prompt |
| Confirmation | OK and DURESS show the **identical** green double-blink |

Timing choices are deliberately slower than Android's 300 ms double-tap / 400 ms long-press defaults ([AOSP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base/main/core/java/android/view/ViewConfiguration.java)), because squeezes may be slow or impaired.

### 5.3 Challenge-response (REMINDED stage)
- The server picks N from **{1, 3}**. Leaving out 2 means a reflex "OK" double squeeze can never pass.
- The device blinks N times, 250 ms on and 350 ms off.
- A press during the blinks, or within 300 ms after them, is invalid and the device re-blinks once.
- The response window is 10 s (configurable to 30 s). If the count equals N, the result is OK, or DURESS if the last press was LONG. A wrong count gets one retry with a new N.
- The device re-blinks every 15 s until the server state changes. **The server countdown is the safety net, not this timer.**

### 5.4 Fall candidate (wrist and hair)

States: IDLE → WAIT_IMPACT → WAIT_STILL → LONG_LIE. Sources: AN-1023, Kangas/Bourke via [Bagalà](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3353905/), wrist evidence from [UMAFall](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5982860/).

- **Free-fall start:** SVM below 0.6 g for 60 ms or more, or the hardware FREE_FALL bit. Also accept an impact with no clear free-fall if SVM dipped below 0.8 g in the previous second.
- **Impact:** SVM of 3.0 g or more within 1000 ms. Trunk literature puts impact thresholds at 2.8–3.52 g, with real impacts around 7 g ([Laguna](https://www.scitepress.org/Papers/2010/29181/29181.pdf)), which is why the range is ±16 g.
- **Dance context:** when the 5-s mean ENMO stays at or above 100 mg for 60 s or more, the impact threshold rises to 4.0 g and the stillness window to 3 s ([ENMO cut-points](https://sportsmedicine-open.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s40798-025-00820-1/tables/4)).
- **Stillness:** within 3.5 s, find a 2 s window where |SVM − 1| < 0.1875 and the SD is below 0.05. Then compute the orientation change as dθ = acos(ĝpre·ĝpost) ([AN3461 Eq. 45](https://www.nxp.jp/docs/en/application-note/AN3461.pdf)):
  - dθ ≥ 45°, or in hair mode a tilt from upright ≥ 60° → HIGH
  - dθ ≥ 20° → MED
  - Still moving after 3.5 s → log `impact_with_recovery` only. This is the dancing and jumping case.
- **LONG_LIE:** 10 s still raises the check-in's priority. It is still only a check-in.

### 5.5 Head-drop (hair mode)

**Calibration:**
- 5 s upright gives `g_ref`.
- 5 s looking at a phone gives θ_phone.
- θ_drop = max(θ_phone + 15°, 50°). People flex the head 33–45° to look at phones ([Lee 2015](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:25323467%20AND%20SRC:MED&resultType=core&format=json)), and maximum active flexion is about 58° ([norms](https://avesis.iku.edu.tr/yayin/e6a38307-12a9-4526-9d9f-efa478dba5e1/normative-values-for-cervical-and-lumbar-range-of-motion-in-healthy-young-adults)).

**Measurement:**
- Measure the angle only when the reading is quasi-static (| |a| − 1 g | < 0.1 g).
- Use the angle between the low-passed gravity vector and `g_ref`. Euler angles are unreliable because the scrunchie's mounting orientation is arbitrary ([AN3461](https://www.nxp.jp/docs/en/application-note/AN3461.pdf)).

**Triggers** (patterns follow [US10964190B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US10964190B2/en); these are precedents, not validated cut-offs):

| Trigger | Condition | Severity | Demo profile |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sustained | forward, θ ≥ θ_drop, low motion, ≥ 20 s | MED | — |
| Nodding | 3 or more drop/recover cycles in 120 s | MED | — |
| Fast drop | ≥ 50°/s ending past θ_drop, held ≥ 10 s | HIGH | **held 5 s** |

All of these are suppressed while walking or in dance context.

### 5.6 Sway (hair mode only; **first thing to cut**)
- Detect walking with 4-s windows: autocorrelation step peak at a lag of 0.35–0.75 s, r ≥ 0.4.
- Feature: ML RMSR, which does not depend on walking speed ([Sekine](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3882286/)).
- Trigger when, over 3 windows, RMSR ≥ max(μ + 3σ, 1.26μ) **and** ML RMS ≥ 1.5× baseline. The cut-offs come from the 26% and 41% smallest detectable differences ([PMC5017322](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5017322/)).
- A personal baseline is required, because population models were not accurate ([Suffoletto 2020](https://www.federvini.it/images/jsad.2020.81.505.pdf)).
- UI wording: "gait looks unusual for you."

### 5.7 Prolonged stillness (second cut)
- Flag when no 5-s epoch angle changes by more than 5° and ENMO stays below 45 mg for **10 min**.
- Shorten to 3 min if any flag fired in the last 30 min.
- Specificity to wakefulness is only 45–65% ([van Hees 2015](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4646630/)), so it only triggers a check-in.

### 5.8 Heart-rate read (on the laptop, not the firmware)

`/hr-bridge` runs on `http://localhost:3000`, which counts as a secure context ([Chrome](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/bluetooth)):
- Call `navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({filters:[{services:['heart_rate']}]})` from a click.
- Then `device.gatt.connect()` → `getPrimaryService('heart_rate')` → `getCharacteristic('heart_rate_measurement')` → `startNotifications()`.
- Reconnect with backoff on `gattserverdisconnected`.

Parsing follows the 0x2A37 layout ([SimpleBLE](https://docs.simpleble.org/recipes/heart-rate-monitor)):

```js
function parseHRM(dv) {                       // DataView of 0x2A37 notification
  const f = dv.getUint8(0); let i = 1;
  const bpm = (f & 0x01) ? dv.getUint16(i, true) : dv.getUint8(i); i += (f & 0x01) ? 2 : 1;
  if (f & 0x08) i += 2;                        // skip Energy Expended
  const rr = [];
  if (f & 0x10) for (; i + 1 < dv.byteLength; i += 2) rr.push(dv.getUint16(i, true) * 1000 / 1024);
  const rrSynthetic = rr.length > 0 && rr.every(r => Math.abs(r - 60000 / bpm) <= 1); // faked RR check
  return { bpm, rr_ms: rr, rr_synthetic: rrSynthetic };
}
```

- The fake-RR check follows [Rutenberg](https://www.guyrutenberg.com/2026/04/04/web-hr-monitor-heart-rate-and-hrv-in-the-browser/).
- POST `{ts, bpm, rr_ms, rr_synthetic, source:'apple_watch_heartcast', simulated:false}` once a second.
- **Stretch only:** an ESP32 NimBLE client subscribed to 0x2A37 ([NimBLE-Arduino](https://github.com/h2zero/NimBLE-Arduino)). Wi-Fi and BLE share one radio by time-division ([Espressif](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/api-guides/coexist.html)).

### 5.9 Heartbeat, telemetry and event protocol

```
POST /v1/device/heartbeat   every 5 s (demo) / 15 s (real)
  hdr: X-Device-Id, X-Boot-Id, X-Seq, X-Ts, X-Sig = hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, ts|seq|body))
  body: {wear_mode, rssi, fsr_base_mv, feats:[{t, svm_mean, svm_sd, svm_min, svm_max, enmo_mg, tilt_deg,
          fwd_flex_deg, quasi_static, walking, ml_rmsr, still_s, int_bits}, ... up to 5]}
  reply: {state_public, server_time, cmd:{led, blink_n, challenge_id, nudge}}
POST /v1/device/events      immediately; event_id = boot_id:seq; retry 1,2,4,8 s with same id
  body: {event_id, type, payload, device_ts}
```

- `WiFi.setSleep(false)` lowers latency.
- iPhone hotspots drop idle third-party clients after 90 s ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/guide/platform-support/sup025284ac0)). The 5 s heartbeat keeps the link alive.
- Turn on **Maximize Compatibility** so the hotspot uses 2.4 GHz, which the ESP32 needs.
- Store two SSIDs in NVS.
- TLS: `setCACert` with the root that `openssl s_client -showcerts` reports. If that fails at 3 a.m., use `setInsecure()` and disclose it ([NetworkClientSecure](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/master/libraries/NetworkClientSecure/README.md)).
- Keep the server URL in `Preferences` and make it settable over serial (`URL https://…`), so a new tunnel URL never needs a reflash.
- **`state_public` never reveals DURESS_SILENT.** It reads ARMED.

### 5.10 Offline buffering
- After 2 failed heartbeats, the device goes offline. The blue LED gives one short flash every 10 s.
- Events are queued in a 32-entry RAM ring. Duress, OK and challenge events are also persisted to NVS through `Preferences`, so they survive a reboot.
- Local check-in prompts continue on the device.
- On reconnect, the device flushes oldest first with the original `device_ts`, and duress events go first.
- On the server:
  - Escalation keeps running during the outage, and a lease expiry opens LOST_CONTACT.
  - A late OK **does not auto-cancel** an escalation. Contacts get "Maya responded at 21:15 (delivered late due to connection)."

### 6.2 State machine

`sessions.state` holds the main state. `sessions.link_state` is a separate field. Every transition is a guarded `UPDATE sessions SET state=$to, version=version+1 WHERE id=$id AND version=$v AND state = ANY($from)`; if zero rows change, the request is stale and ignored.

| From | Trigger | To | Side effects | Deadline demo / real |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARMED | CHECKIN_DUE, or **PULL_FORWARD** (sensor/HR) | PROMPTED | `cmd.led=amber_pulse`; Telegram nudge to the wearer's chat (watch taps) | 10 s / 2 min |
| PROMPTED | `squeeze_ok` or PWA "I'm OK" | ARMED | Schedule next CHECKIN_DUE | Interval 120 s / user preset (e.g. 30 min) |
| PROMPTED | PROMPT_TIMEOUT | REMINDED | `challenge_n ∈ {1,3}`; `cmd.blink_n` | 10 s / 2 min |
| REMINDED | Correct `challenge_reply` | ARMED | — | — |
| REMINDED | REMINDER_TIMEOUT | **ESCALATED_L1** | Alert NO_RESPONSE; outbox to priority 1; location share (simulated coordinates) expiring after 90 s / 60 min | Ack 15 s / 5 min |
| ESCALATED_L1 | ACK_TIMEOUT_L1 | **ESCALATED_L2** | Notify priority 2 (judge page) and re-ping #1; RENOTIFY every 20 s / 60 s, capped at 10 | — |
| L1 / L2 | First ack (Telegram or web) | RESOLVED | "<name> is handling it" to the others; `editMessageText` | — |
| PROMPTED / REMINDED / L1 / L2 | Real PIN in the PWA, or a passed challenge after escalation | FALSE_ALARM | "False alarm: Maya cancelled with her PIN at 21:17" to everyone already notified | — |
| Any active state | Duress squeeze or duress PIN | **DURESS_SILENT** (device and PWA see ARMED / "Cancelled ✓") | Alert DURESS to #1 immediately: "SILENT HELP REQUEST. She may not be able to talk. Don't call her phone." | Ack 10 s / 2 min, then L2 |
| DURESS_SILENT | Real PIN | Unchanged | Note to contacts: "Maya entered her cancel PIN. Please confirm in person." Only a contact's ack closes it | — |
| `link_state` OK | `lease_expires_at < now()` (lease 12 s / 60 s) | `link_state = LOST_CONTACT` | Alert LOST_CONTACT: "Lost contact with Maya's device (battery or signal?). This is NOT a missed check-in." Pending deadlines **keep running** | — |

The real-mode PIN and duress responses must be **byte-identical**.

### 6.3 Schema
Plain tables:
- users
- devices (`hmac_secret`, `boot_id`, `last_seq`, `lease_expires_at`)
- contacts (`priority`, `channel`, `telegram_chat_id`, `web_token_hash`, `invite_token`, `invite_expires_at`, `verified_at`, `revoked_at`)
- sessions (`state`, `link_state`, `version`, profile timings, `challenge_n`)
- timers
- alerts
- outbox (`dedupe_key UNIQUE`, `provider_message_id`)
- acks (`telegram_update_id UNIQUE`)
- device_events (`event_id` PK, cached `result`)
- audit_log
- location_shares
- bot_state
- user_baselines

These stay out of hypertables because a hypertable's unique keys must include the time column ([Tiger](https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/use-timescale/latest/hypertables/hypertables-and-unique-indexes)).

```sql
CREATE TABLE hr_samples (
  time timestamptz NOT NULL, user_id uuid NOT NULL, source text NOT NULL,
  simulated boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, bpm smallint NOT NULL,
  rr_ms real[], rr_synthetic boolean
) WITH (tsdb.hypertable = true, tsdb.partition_column = 'time',
        tsdb.segmentby = 'user_id', tsdb.chunk_interval = '1 day');
-- motion_features: (time, device_id, wear_mode, svm_mean, svm_sd, enmo_mg, tilt_deg, ml_rmsr, still_s, fsr_a, fsr_b), segmentby device_id

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW hr_1m WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
  SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', time) AS bucket, user_id, simulated,
         avg(bpm) AS avg_bpm, stddev(bpm) AS sd_bpm, min(bpm) AS min_bpm, max(bpm) AS max_bpm, count(*) AS n
  FROM hr_samples GROUP BY bucket, user_id, simulated;
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('hr_1m', start_offset => INTERVAL '1 day',
       end_offset => INTERVAL '1 minute', schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 minute');
ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW hr_1m SET (timescaledb.materialized_only = false);
SELECT add_retention_policy('hr_samples',      drop_after => INTERVAL '48 hours');
SELECT add_retention_policy('motion_features', drop_after => INTERVAL '48 hours');

CREATE INDEX timers_due ON timers (fire_at) WHERE fired_at IS NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL;
```

- Syntax: `tsdb.*` needs TimescaleDB 2.20 or later; otherwise use `create_hypertable` ([docs](https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/api/latest/hypertable/create_table)). Continuous aggregates: ([caggs](https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/reference/timescaledb/continuous-aggregates)).
- The cagg's 1-day refresh window is shorter than the 48 h retention, so dropping raw chunks never wipes the aggregate.
- **audit_log** columns: `prev_hash`, `hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical_json(row))`, chained per session. `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` from the app role, plus a `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger that raises an error.
- User erasure runs as the owner role and leaves a tombstone: "log erased by user at T".

### 6.4 Timer worker and outbox

```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT id, session_id, kind, expected_version FROM timers
 WHERE fired_at IS NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL AND fire_at <= now()
 ORDER BY fire_at LIMIT 20 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;
-- per timer: SELECT ... FROM sessions WHERE id=$s FOR UPDATE; guarded UPDATE; INSERT next timer;
-- INSERT INTO outbox ... ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING; INSERT audit_log; UPDATE timers SET fired_at=now()
COMMIT;
```

- Use the database's `now()` as the only clock.
- `SKIP LOCKED` makes N workers safe ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html)).
- A `kill -9` before COMMIT rolls back the whole transition, and the next process redoes it from the stored deadline.
- **Outbox sender:**
  - Claim rows: `UPDATE outbox SET status='sending', locked_until=now()+'30 s' WHERE id IN (SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 10) RETURNING *`.
  - Send, then mark `sent` with the Telegram `message_id`.
  - A reaper resets stale `sending` rows.
  - On HTTP 429, set `next_attempt_at = now() + retry_after`. Send at most 1 message/s per chat ([Bot FAQ](https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq)).
  - Delivery is **at least once**. Tell judges this is the deliberate safety trade-off.

### 6.6 Heart-rate rule (output is PULL_FORWARD only)

All thresholds below are engineering assumptions that need validation.

- **Baseline:** median `avg_bpm` from `hr_1m` over a 5-minute calibration, with `simulated = false`, stored in `user_baselines`.
- **Every 10 s:** compute the 60 s median from `hr_samples`.
- **Fire** when |median − baseline| ≥ max(30 bpm, 35%) for **90 s** (15 s in the demo profile) **and** mean ENMO over 60 s is below 45 mg, so the wearer is still.
- Result: `PULL_FORWARD(reason='hr_shift_from_baseline', MED)`, with a 15-minute cooldown.
- HR signal lost for more than 120 s while armed: one PULL_FORWARD at LOW.

Rationale for judges:
- Alcohol raises heart rate and lowers HRV ([JMIR](https://mental.jmir.org/2018/1/e23)).
- GHB caused bradycardia in 38% of 65 and 36% of 88 emergency cases ([SMW](https://smw.ch/index.php/smw/article/download/409/406/806)).
- So a change in heart rate is **non-specific** and only means "ask sooner."
- HRV: compute RMSSD over a rolling 60 s window only if real, non-synthetic RR is present ([PMC5624990](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5624990/)). Otherwise label it "simulated / roadmap."

### 6.7 Telegram flows
- **Create the bot** with @BotFather ([features](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features)). Call `deleteWebhook` once, then long-poll `getUpdates(timeout=25, allowed_updates=['message','callback_query'])`. Store the offset in `bot_state` in the same transaction that processes the update ([Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api)).
- **Invite:**
  - `https://t.me/<bot>?start=<token>`, where the token is `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)`, single use, 24 h expiry. Deep-link parameters allow up to 64 characters ([features](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features)).
  - On `/start <token>`, bind the `chat_id`. A bot cannot message someone who has never started it ([Sinch](https://support.sinch.com/hc/en-us/articles/54629170811027-Is-it-possible-to-use-a-Telegram-Bot-to-send-campaign-or-regular-updates-to-Telegram-users)), so **every team phone runs /start before demo prep**.
  - Reply: "You're Maya's trusted contact #1. You'll see nothing from StillHere unless she misses check-ins or asks for help."
- **Alert:**
  - `sendMessage` with `protect_content=true`.
  - Text: "StillHere: Maya hasn't responded to 2 check-ins (21:14, 21:14). This is not a confirmed emergency. Location (expires 21:16): <link>".
  - `reply_markup = {"inline_keyboard":[[{"text":"I'm on it (Acknowledge)","callback_data":"ack:<alert>:<contact>"}],[{"text":"Open live page","url":"https://<tunnel>/c/<token>"}]]}`. `callback_data` is limited to 64 bytes, so use short IDs.
- **Ack:**
  1. INSERT into acks (unique on `update_id`).
  2. Compare-and-set the alert as acknowledged.
  3. `answerCallbackQuery("Acknowledged, others notified")`.
  4. `editMessageText` to "Acknowledged by <name> at 21:16".
  5. Fan out "<name> is handling it" to the other contacts.

### 6.8 QR contact page (the judge as Contact #2)
1. Before the pitch, the operator console creates an invite and shows its QR on screen and on a printed card.
2. `/c/<token>` shows one consent screen: "You'll see nothing unless Maya misses check-ins. Tap to become Contact #2."
3. **That tap:**
   - Starts a looping `<audio>` alarm element with `muted=true`. Audio elements ignore the mute switch, while Web Audio is "ambient" on iOS and obeys it ([WebKit 237322](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=237322)).
   - Sets `navigator.audioSession.type='playback'` when available ([WebKit 251532](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=251532)).
   - Resumes an AudioContext ([Chrome autoplay](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/autoplay)).
   - Requests a screen Wake Lock, which is released if the page is hidden ([wake lock](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/wake-lock)).
   - POSTs `/join`.
4. The page polls status every second.
5. **On an alert:** full-screen red, unmute the alarm, `navigator.vibrate` (Android only; it does nothing on iOS, per [bugnet](https://bugnet.io/blog/fix-web-game-vibrate-api-not-available-ios-safari)), and a big **Acknowledge** button.
6. Ask the judge to keep the page in front. Have a spare "judge phone" ready.

### 6.9 Chaos and reliability tests (script in `tests/chaos.sh`, run at 03:30 and 05:00)

| Test | How | Pass criterion |
|---|---|---|
| `kill -9` mid-REMINDED | `pkill -9 -f uvicorn`; restart loop | L1 fires ≤ 2 s after the stored `fire_at`; exactly one Telegram message |
| Crash between send and mark | Inject an exception after the HTTP 200 | At most one duplicate (documented) |
| Two workers, two laptops | Both point at Tiger | Each timer fired once (`fired_at` set once; `dedupe_key` unique) |
| Event replay | Same `event_id` ×5 | One transition; identical cached responses |
| Duress indistinguishable | Diff OK vs duress responses (HTTP and device `cmd`) | Byte-identical; timing padded to ±50 ms |
| Unplug device | Pull power | LOST_CONTACT within lease + 1 s, with its own wording; a pending deadline still fires as NO_RESPONSE |
| Telegram 429 | Mock it | `next_attempt_at` honoured |
| Tunnel down | Stop cloudflared for 30 s | ESP32 buffers and flushes; Telegram unaffected |
| DB unreachable | Wrong `DATABASE_URL` | 503s; device retries; no lost events after recovery |
| **Core rule** | Unit test over all transitions | No code path from a sensor or HR event to `ESCALATED_*` |
| Privacy | Status before an alert; location after expiry | No session fields; 410 |
| Wording | `grep -riE "spiked|intoxicat|unconscious|diagnos"` over UI strings | Zero hits |

**Q&A cheat sheet (1 minute):**
- **"Why not just Apple's fall detection?"** It auto-calls services and has produced floods of false calls ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/1473802/apple-acknowledges-faulty-crash-detection-skiers.html)). We ask the person first, then call people, not 911.
- **"False alarm rate?"** Even the best threshold detector produced about 5 false alarms a day ([Bagalà](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3353905/)). That is why a false trigger costs only a squeeze.
- **"What if someone takes the scrunchie off?"** Its link drops, the lost-contact alert fires, and any running countdown keeps going.
- **"What if she's asleep?"** Contacts escalate after missed check-ins. The wearer sets the cadence and can disarm.
- **"Why Telegram?"** Native push and watch mirroring at no messaging cost to us. SMS trials only reach verified numbers ([Twilio](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/guides/how-to-use-your-free-trial-account)).
- **"How does the duress squeeze stay hidden?"** Same blink, same API bytes, and it's hidden from the on-phone log until resolved.

verdict:
This is a strong KAZE entry, and it is fixable in time. The core safety design matches the brief closely. Sensors only pull a check-in forward, escalation is server-side and survives crashes, duress looks like a cancel, lost contact is a separate alert, contacts see nothing before an alert, and simulated items are labelled. A judge would also give credit for the honest demonstrated/simulated table (§9).

My estimate as the KAZE judge is about 70/100 as written, and 85+ with the fixes below.

What costs points:
- **Scope (feasibility).** About 13 hours with naps is not enough for everything listed.
- **Safety-logic gaps (25%).** One acknowledge tap closes the alert. Escalation has no final step. A reflex double squeeze passes the first sensor-triggered prompt. Accidental silent duress is likely from pressure on the scrunchie.
- **Hair-mode usability (20%).** The wearer cannot see LEDs on the back of her head, but people around her can.
- **Privacy (10%).** Anyone who scans the QR becomes a contact without the wearer approving. Continuous posture and heart-rate telemetry goes to the cloud. Real alert-time location is impossible from a web page while the phone is locked.
- **Credibility.**
  - The Q&A says taking the scrunchie off drops its link. That is false.
  - The GHB bradycardia numbers do not match the cited paper.
  - The Statistics Canada claim comes from a 2018 article.
  - There is no answer to Apple Check In or Google Safety Check, which the big-tech judges will raise.

Facts I checked that hold up:
- HeartCast is free, v3.9.0, needs iOS 18.6+ and watchOS 8.0+, and "will continue to run in the background during your workout" (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/heartcast-heart-rate-monitor/id1499771124). Locking the iPhone after Chrome connects is fine.
- The Fitbit Charge 6 shares heart rate with one app or machine at a time (https://support.google.com/fitbit/answer/14236705).
- The legacy Fitbit Web API shuts down Oct 30, 2026 (https://developers.google.com/health/reference/rest/v4/users?hl=id). Using the Fitbit only as Contact #1's wrist buzzer is the right call.
- Cloudflare quick tunnels allow 200 in-flight requests and do not support SSE (https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/). The 1 s polling design is fine.
- In Bagalà 2012, mean sensitivity on 29 real falls was 57%, and the best algorithm (Bourke3) gave about 5 false alarms a day (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3353905/). The plan's numbers are correct.

problems.problem: The scope does not fit about 13 hours of build time with naps, and KAZE is judged on what was built. The firmware alone covers ADXL345 FIFO burst reads, the squeeze decoder, the challenge, a fall state machine, head-drop, sway, stillness, NVS offline persistence, HMAC and TLS. On top of that come the backend state machine, outbox, Telegram, PWA, dashboard, heart-rate bridge and chaos script. The current cut list only starts cutting 'if behind', so the team is likely to arrive at 03:30 with many half-working modules.
problems.fix:
1. **Cut now:** sway, prolonged stillness, chest-strap HRV, Fitbit as a heart-rate source, and the GoDaddy domain.
2. **Detectors:** build only head-drop for real. Hair mode is the hook. The fall becomes an operator injection labelled 'fall-like motion (simulated)'.
3. **Must work by 23:30:** real FSR OK/duress, head-drop, the live heart-rate data path, server timers through L1/L2 with acknowledgement and lost contact, the judge page, and the dashboard.
4. **Security:** use a bearer token instead of HMAC, and `setInsecure()` instead of CA pinning (disclose it in §9).
5. **Hardware fallback:** if the ESP32 has not been flashed by 19:00, switch to Plan B (Uno) with no debate.
6. **Score the real work:** anything that is merely configured goes in §9 as 'configured', not 'demonstrated'.

problems.problem: The 4-minute demo is overpacked. It runs 7 scenarios plus the QR join, `kill -9`, unplugging and the privacy beat in 240 s. The '30-second pitch' is about 125 words, roughly 55 s at 140 wpm, but the script gives it 20 s. Scenario 2 alone has 35 s of timers (10 + 10 + 15 s) before the judge's phone fires. Running over 4:00 costs the presentation, and it loses the Q&A minute where safety questions get answered.
problems.fix:
1. Cut the pitch to about 60 words.
2. Run scenarios 1, 3 and 2+5+4 (`kill -9`) live, in about 2:15.
3. Unplug the device during the L1 wait. The 12 s lease expires inside the 15 s ack window, so the connectivity beat costs no extra time.
4. Give scenario 6 (false alarm, with a pre-staged fast-forward) and scenario 7 (410 link plus export) 10 s each.
5. Rehearse three times with a stopwatch, aiming for 3:40.

problems.problem: Acknowledging is treated as resolving. One reflexive tap on 'I'm on it' from a half-asleep Contact #1 sets the alert to RESOLVED, and nobody else is ever told. KAZE asks for escalation when the first contact does not acknowledge. The real failure is an acknowledgement with no action behind it.
problems.fix:
1. Add an ACKED state between L1/L2 and RESOLVED. After acknowledging, the contact must tap either 'I'm with her / she's safe' or 'Can't reach her' within a follow-up timer (20 s demo, 10 min real). If they don't, the alert re-escalates to the next contact and re-pings the first.
2. Add an 'I can't help, pass it on' button that escalates immediately. That saves up to 5 minutes in real mode.
3. Unit-test that only 'she's safe' or the PIN reaches RESOLVED.

problems.problem: Escalation dead-ends. After L2, contacts are re-notified up to 10 times and then nothing happens, so a night where both contacts are asleep ends silently. By comparison, Google's Safety Check automatically starts Emergency Sharing, with live location to contacts, when there is no response (https://support.google.com/assistant/answer/13683607).
problems.fix:
1. Add an ESCALATED_FINAL state that is reached only when every contact has failed to respond.
2. Show a red 'Emergency services: SIMULATED – would contact 911 / campus safety with last known location' on the dashboard and contact page, and log it.
3. Never place a call.
4. List this state as simulated in §9.

problems.problem: A reflex squeeze defeats the first sensor-triggered prompt. The 1-or-3 blink challenge only applies at REMINDED, so a reflexive [S,S] at PROMPTED returns the session to ARMED. The next check-in is then 30 minutes away, which is exactly the missed signal the challenge was meant to prevent. Worst-case time to the first alert becomes the check-in interval plus 4 minutes, even after a head-drop flag. With only {1,3}, a guess passes 50% of the time.
problems.fix:
1. When PROMPTED was caused by PULL_FORWARD (a sensor or heart-rate flag), require the challenge at the first prompt. Accept a plain [S,S] only for routine scheduled check-ins.
2. Draw N from {1,3,4} to cut the guess rate to 33%.
3. Put the worst-case latency on a slide: scheduled check-ins = interval + 2 + 2 min; sensor-flagged = about 4 min.

problems.problem:
Silent duress will fire by accident. Any [S…,L] pattern with a hold of 1000 ms or more counts as duress in any active state.
- In hair mode, leaning back on a booth or car headrest, lying on a couch, a hug, or a hat compresses the ponytail scrunchie for more than 1 s.
- In wrist mode, gripping a glass or bag strap does the same.
- Impaired, slow squeezes run close to 1 s, and reaction time slows with alcohol (https://sk.pf.jcu.cz/artkey/stk-201603-0018_vliv-alkoholu-na-zmenu-reakcni-doby-u-muzu.php).

Because duress looks exactly like a cancel, the wearer never learns that she sent 'SILENT HELP REQUEST… Don't call her phone.' That is the highest-severity false alarm, and she has no visible way to correct it.
problems.fix:
1. Make duress more deliberate: three short squeezes then a hold of at least 2 s ([S,S,S,L≥2 s]), and require both FSRs to rise together (a pinch across the band).
2. Reject candidates during large orientation changes or steady pressure on both FSRs (head on a headrest).
3. Outside the 20 s after a prompt, accept duress only after a deliberate wake pattern.
4. Replay the recorded dance, sit-back and lie-down traces through the decoder and report the false-duress count in §9.
5. Keep the duress PIN in the PWA as the primary duress path.

problems.problem: The plan contradicts itself on late responses. It says 'Real PIN or a passed challenge after escalation → FALSE_ALARM', but also says 'A late OK does not auto-cancel.' Under the first rule, a semi-responsive person who briefly rouses and squeezes back 3 stands down every contact while she may still be in danger.
problems.fix:
1. After any ESCALATED state, a device squeeze should only downgrade the alert: 'Maya responded on her device at 21:17 – please still check on her.'
2. Only the PWA PIN, which is cognitively harder, or a contact's 'she's safe' closes the alert.
3. Make the two rules consistent in the state table and in the unit test.

problems.problem: Hair mode breaks the visual design. The wearer cannot see LEDs at the back of her head, so the amber prompt and the 1–3 blink challenge are invisible to her. Meanwhile LEDs blinking in a dark venue are visible to everyone nearby, including the person she may be afraid of. That undermines both discretion and the claim that duress looks the same as a cancel. The demo is staged in hair mode, so a judge will ask about this.
problems.fix:
1. In hair mode, turn the LEDs off, except a single dim LED during setup.
2. Deliver the prompt as the watch tap: the Telegram nudge reaches the Apple Watch when the iPhone is locked (https://support.apple.com/en-us/108369).
3. Carry the challenge number in neutral notification text such as 'Reminder 3', or as N separate nudges. She squeezes back N.
4. Keep LED blinks for wrist mode only, and say this out loud during the demo.

problems.problem: One Q&A answer is false: 'What if someone takes the scrunchie off? Its link drops.' A scrunchie lying on a table keeps sending heartbeats. An engineer judge will catch this, and it undermines everything else the team says. For comparison, Apple Check In treats 'Apple Watch removal' as a signal it shares (https://support.apple.com/en-au/guide/personal-safety/ips56b5bc469/web).
problems.fix:
1. Build an off-body flag that costs about 30 minutes. If the FSR baseline drops well below its calibrated band and there is no motion for 60 s, raise PULL_FORWARD with reason 'device may be off'.
2. Treat the watch's heart-rate stream stopping under the existing 'heart-rate lost' rule.
3. If neither is built, the Q&A answer is: 'The prototype doesn't detect removal; that's on the roadmap.'

problems.problem:
The plan doesn't answer the obvious comparison. Big-tech judges will ask how this differs from two built-in features:
- **Apple Check In** (iOS 17+): if you don't respond, it sends a contact your location, battery and signal. The full option adds your route, last iPhone unlock and Apple Watch removal (https://support.apple.com/en-au/guide/personal-safety/ips56b5bc469/web).
- **Google Safety Check:** if you don't respond, it starts Emergency Sharing, sending live location to your contacts. A check can last up to 24 h (https://support.google.com/assistant/answer/13683607).

The impact story (30%) is weaker without a clear differentiation.

Real alert-time location is not possible from a web page. The W3C Geolocation spec (§6.5 step 5) makes a position request wait while the page is hidden and pauses `watchPosition` updates (https://www.w3.org/TR/geolocation/). At alert time the wearer is unresponsive and her phone is locked in a pocket, so 'location shared only at alert time' is not achievable from the PWA. The plan also expires the location link after a fixed 60 minutes in real mode, which could cut off a contact who is still searching.
problems.fix:
1. Add this limit to §9 as an assumption to validate.
2. Prototype design: capture last-known location whenever she interacts (arming, or 'I'm OK' in the PWA). Store it encrypted and release it only at alert time, showing its age ('as of 21:02, 14 min old').
3. Real version: a native app with background location (roadmap).
4. Keep the link valid while the alert is open plus 30 minutes after 'she's safe', then return 410. Never keep location history.

problems.problem: The contact invite flow enables stalking. Opening `/c/<token>` or the t.me invite makes the person a contact with no approval from the wearer. A photographed QR code, or a controlling partner holding the link, gains future alert and location access. Nothing defines who can arm a session, see its status, or remove a contact. That is a misuse risk under privacy and autonomy (10%).
problems.fix:
1. The wearer approves every join in the PWA: 'Approve Judge as Contact #2?' with one tap. Showing this in the demo scores autonomy points.
2. Contacts can never arm a session, see status or request location.
3. The wearer can remove a contact silently, with no notification.
4. Show a 'who can be alerted' list every time she arms.
5. Make invite tokens single-use with a 10-minute expiry.
6. Name coercive control explicitly on the privacy slide.

problems.problem:
The heart-rate story overclaims and the statistics are wrong.
- The plan says GHB caused bradycardia in '38% of 65 and 36% of 88' cases. The cited paper (Liechti & Kupferschmidt, Swiss Med Wkly 2004;134:534–537) reports bradycardia below 55/min in 30% of n=141 (Switzerland), 20% of n=104 (Barcelona) and 35% of n=88 (San Francisco) (https://smw.ch/index.php/smw/article/download/409/406/806).
- Putting GHB bradycardia next to a heart-rate rule invites the reading 'it detects GHB', which is a KAZE red line.
- The rule (a change of at least 30 bpm or 35% for 90 s while still) will fire mostly on recovery after dancing, when heart rate stays high while she sits, or on anxiety.
- The baseline is taken at arming, which may be mid-party.
problems.fix:
1. Correct the numbers.
2. Keep GHB physiology off the slides and use it only if asked in Q&A.
3. Suppress the heart-rate rule for 10 minutes after ENMO has been at least 100 mg.
4. Take the baseline from a calibration before going out.
5. Label the rule an untested engineering assumption in §9.
6. In the UI, say 'heart rate different from your usual'. Never say 'bradycardia' or 'tachycardia'.

problems.problem: The opening statistic is eight years old. Global News (Aug 2, 2018) quotes a Statistics Canada spokeswoman saying 'administering a noxious thing' is wrapped into 'other assaults' (https://globalnews.ca/news/4367269/n-s-police-to-review-drink-tampering/amp). Stated as present-day fact, it can be challenged in Q&A.
problems.fix:
1. Say 'As of 2018, Statistics Canada couldn't separate spiking from other assaults.'
2. Add current contrast: UK police received 6,732 spiking reports between May 2022 and April 2023. The UK now has a dedicated administering-a-harmful-substance offence covering spiking, after the Crime and Policing Act received Royal Assent on 29 Apr 2026 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/crime-and-policing-bill-2025-factsheets/crime-and-policing-bill-spiking-factsheet-moj).
3. Add that 7.8% of 6,064 US students reported being drugged (https://www.apa.org/news/press/releases/2016/05/drink-spiking).
4. Use the same Swiss paper for the incident log's value: there is no rapid screen for GHB, which becomes undetectable in blood within 4–8 h and in urine after at most 12 h.

problems.problem:
The privacy claims are stronger than the data handling.
- 1 Hz feature rows (posture, forward flex, gait, stillness, FSR) and 1 Hz heart rate stream to the cloud all night, even when nothing is wrong.
- The `hr_1m` and `motion_1m` continuous aggregates have no retention, so aggregates outlive the 48 h raw policy.
- 'Delete my data' cannot simply DELETE from a continuous aggregate. Tiger's docs say refreshing an aggregate over deleted raw data deletes the matching aggregate data, and that retention can be applied to the aggregate itself (https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/use-timescale/latest/data-retention/data-retention-with-continuous-aggregates).
problems.fix:
1. In the real profile, send only lease heartbeats and events. Stream full features only in a badged 'demo/debug telemetry' profile.
2. Add `add_retention_policy` on both aggregates (for example 7 days).
3. Implement erase as: delete the user's raw rows, then `refresh_continuous_aggregate` over that user's window.
4. Create the Tiger service in ca-central-1 (https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/learn/tiger-cloud/regions) and say 'health data stays in Canada'.

problems.problem: 'Tamper-evident log' is an overclaim. The server holds the hash chain, so the operator could recompute it after an edit. The log could also be misread later, for example 'she squeezed OK at 22:00' taken to mean she was fine.
problems.fix:
1. Say 'hash-chained; edits after export are detectable'.
2. Anchor the head hash by sending it to the wearer's own Telegram chat at the end of each session.
3. Call it a 'personal timeline', not evidence.
4. Label entries 'device response', not wellbeing.
5. Auto-delete after 30 days unless the user pins it.

problems.problem: Lost-contact alerts will be noisy in real use, and the wording is risky. A 60 s lease over a phone hotspot in a crowded venue will page contacts often. The text '(battery or signal?)' downplays deliberate removal by an attacker.
problems.fix:
1. In the real profile, nudge the wearer first.
2. Notify contacts only if contact isn't restored within 5 minutes, or if a check-in comes due in the meantime.
3. Use neutral wording: 'We lost contact with Maya's device at 21:14. Cause unknown. Her check-in schedule is still running.'

problems.problem: Session end is undefined. 'Night out: every 30 min until 2 AM' does not say what happens at 2 AM. Auto-disarming opens a gap during the walk home.
problems.fix:
1. Every preset ends with a final 'Home safe?' check-in that escalates normally if missed.
2. Disarm only with the PIN.
3. The 'walking home' preset ends only on PIN or an arrival tap.

problems.problem:
The accessibility claims need tightening.
- WCAG 2.2.1 requires a time limit to be adjustable to at least 10× the default, or extendable with at least a 20 s warning (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/timing-adjustable). Going from 10 s to 30 s is 3×.
- The plan also mentions user testing 'under impairment'. KAZE allows only simulations.
problems.fix:
1. Either make the challenge window adjustable to 100 s and claim 'meets 2.2.1 (adjust)', or drop the citation.
2. State the real window: 2 minutes per stage.
3. Specify that impairment testing is simulated only (gloves, a dual task, impairment goggles), never with intoxicated people.

problems.problem:
Disabling Fall Detection does not remove every way the demo could place a real call. Holding the Apple Watch side button starts a countdown and then dials emergency services automatically (https://support.apple.com/108374).

There is also a demo failure risk. If Fitness Focus is set to 'When starting a workout', the HeartCast workout silences notifications, including the Telegram nudge that is the only prompt in hair mode (https://iphonelife.com/content/how-to-stop-apple-watch-notifications-during-workout).
problems.fix:
Add four items to the T−10 checklist:
1. Turn off 'Hold Side Button to Dial' on the watch.
2. Turn off automatic-call SOS options on all team phones.
3. Set Fitness Focus 'When starting a workout' to OFF.
4. Do a live test: the nudge reaches the watch while HeartCast is running and the iPhone is locked.

problems.problem: 'Contacts need no app (web page)' only holds for the demo. In real life no contact keeps a page open all night. On iOS, web push works only for web apps added to the Home Screen (https://webkit.org/blog/13878/web-push-for-web-apps-on-ios-and-ipados/). Telegram bot chats are cloud chats, encrypted between client and server but not end to end (https://telegram.org/faq).
problems.fix:
1. In §9, state the real-world channels: Telegram, a Home Screen web app with push, and SMS in production.
2. Keep alert text minimal, with no health data, and say why.

problems.problem: Nothing speaks to the sponsor's value lens. The KAZE judge is Head of FinOps & Value Management at BMO, and the plan has no unit economics or adoption path.
problems.fix:
Add one 15-second slide:
- **Bill of materials:** Grove ADXL345 US$10.90 (https://www.seeedstudio.com/Grove-3-Axis-Digital-Accelerometer-16g.html); FSR01CE ₱600.48 each at qty 1, ₱418 at qty 1k (https://www.digikey.ph/en/products/detail/ohmite/FSR01CE/9178296); plus an ESP32.
- **Data per user-night (real profile):** heartbeats every 15 s ≈ 1,440 rows over 6 h; heart rate at 1 Hz ≈ 21,600 rows, compressed.
- **Messaging cost:** $0 on Telegram.

verdict:
The plan can be finished only if about 40% of it is cut before 19:00. The backend core can be built in the time: Postgres timers with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, the outbox, Telegram, the judge QR page, the live kill -9 and the SIMULATED labels. Three areas are over budget or fragile:
- **Firmware scope.** The list runs to about 12 hours for PICkachu: fall, sway, stillness, FIFO/interrupt registers, NVS buffering, HMAC and TLS. The 4-minute script uses none of fall, sway, stillness or NVS buffering.
- **A second web stack.** The plan has a Next.js dashboard and a Next.js PWA, plus the contact page and the HR bridge, all on Cami.
- **An untethered ESP32.** It depends on HTTPS through an iPhone hotspot, a 2.4 GHz band crowded with every other team's devices, and a quick tunnel. Each of these is a separate way for the demo to fail on stage.

There is one hard blocker: there is no confirmed micro-USB data cable, and the MLH lab list has no micro-USB cables, ESP32 or batteries (https://guide.mlh.com/organizer-resources/hardware-lab-contents).

On heart rate, the request names both watches, and the plan's use of each is right:
- **Apple Watch: primary.** Route it through HeartCast to Chrome Web Bluetooth on the laptop. HeartCast is free, with only optional Pro and Audible purchases, and needs iOS 18.6+ and watchOS 8.0+ (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/heartcast-heart-rate-monitor/id1499771124). This path gives heart rate only, not live HRV.
- **Fitbit: only if it is a Charge 6.** Of Fitbit models, only the Charge 6 (plus Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 2+) shares heart rate, and the Charge 6 connects to one device at a time and drains its battery (https://support.google.com/fitbit/answer/14236705). Any other model is more useful as Contact #1's wrist buzzer.

Recommended changes:
- Build hair mode only.
- Make USB serial (bridge.py) the default transport for the scrunchie, with Wi-Fi as an upgrade that must pass a soak test by 01:00.
- Replace Next.js with plain HTML pages served by FastAPI.
- Remove HMAC.

The safety rule (sensors only trigger an earlier check-in), duress, lost contact, L2 escalation and the judge moment all stay.

If upload fails, hold BOOT during upload, or fit the electrolytic capacitor you already have between EN and GND, stripe to GND (10 µF per https://randomnerdtutorials.com/solved-failed-to-connect-to-esp32-timed-out-waiting-for-packet-header/). Seeed sells both the ADXL345 (address 0x53) and the LIS3DHTR (default 0x19; https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/Grove-3-Axis-Digital-Accelerometer-LIS3DHTR/) under that name, and §5.1's register block works only on the ADXL345.

Either way, skip the FIFO and interrupt configuration: the sensing task does a 6-byte burst read every 10 ms and all detection runs in software. That removes the 320 ms FIFO-overflow constraint and about an hour of register debugging.

problems.problem: There is no clean way to connect a Grove module to a bare ESP32. The kit has no Grove-to-female-jumper cable, and the MLH tool list has a wire stripper, cutter, multimeter and pliers but no soldering iron (https://guide.mlh.com/organizer-resources/hardware-lab-contents). Stripped 26 AWG stranded Grove wire pushed into a breadboard is intermittent, so the I2C bus can hang mid-demo. In hair mode the plan also runs I2C from the ponytail down to a wrist pouch, which adds bus capacitance (the I2C spec allows 400 pF; https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/user-guide/UM10204.pdf).
problems.fix: Ask the MLH desk for a Grove-to-female-jumper cable first. Otherwise cut a Grove cable, strip about 10 mm, fold the strands back and push them into the female end of an M/F jumper, then tape or hot-glue the joint. Use Wire.setClock(100000) and Wire.setTimeOut(20), and re-init I2C after 3 consecutive read errors. For hair mode, put the ESP32 in the hair pocket next to the sensor and run only the USB power cable to a power bank in a pocket. Plan B (Uno + Base Shield) avoids cutting entirely, because the module plugs straight into the shield's I2C port.

Blue and white LEDs, and many bright 'green' LEDs, have a forward voltage of about 2.8–3.3 V (https://www.espboards.dev/tools/led-resistor-calculator/). From a 3.3 V GPIO through 220–330 Ω they are dim or off, which affects the GPIO33 blue link LED and possibly the green 'OK' blink.
problems.fix: Borrow the MLH 'Resistor Kit' and check values on its one shared multimeter (https://guide.mlh.com/organizer-resources/hardware-lab-contents). Use red and yellow LEDs with 220 Ω for anything the judges must see. Test blue and green with 47–100 Ω, and if they are still dim, make the OK/duress double-blink yellow. On the Uno, use Grove LED Socket kits instead (MLH has 20, each with a resistor on board).

problems.problem: The iPhone hotspot is fragile for the ESP32. Apple tells you to 'Stay on this screen until you connect your other device' (https://support.apple.com/en-afri/119837). Third-party devices are dropped after 90 s without traffic, and 2.4 GHz needs Maximize Compatibility (https://support.apple.com/guide/platform-support/sup025284ac0). Default hotspot names like 'Name’s iPhone' use a curly apostrophe (U+2019) that does not match the straight apostrophe in firmware strings (https://forum.mdash.net/t/wifi-ssid-limitations-and-scans/508, https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.24/people/AimanAnuar/week13.html). The lost-contact beat power-cycles the ESP32, so 'Contact restored' depends on it rejoining on stage.
problems.fix: Rename the hotspot phone to an ASCII name such as SHDEMO and turn Maximize Compatibility on. Keep that phone plugged in and parked on the Personal Hotspot screen during every demo. Prefer an Android hotspot if a teammate has one. Store two SSIDs. At G6, rehearse unplug and replug 5 times and measure rejoin plus first successful POST; if it exceeds 15 s or fails even once, use serial transport for the demo.

problems.problem: Commands to the device lag, and the lease will raise false alarms. The amber prompt and the challenge blinks only arrive in the reply to a heartbeat sent every 5 s, so they can land 5 s into a 10 s response window. Each POST without keep-alive is a fresh TLS handshake, which Espressif says needs 40–50 KB of free heap (https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-faq/en/latest/software-framework/protocols/esp-tls.html). On congested Wi-Fi, two slow heartbeats exceed the 12 s lease and send judges a spurious LOST_CONTACT.
problems.fix: Demo profile: heartbeat every 1–2 s with HTTP keep-alive (HTTPClient.setReuse(true)), and give the network task at least 12 KB of stack. Start the PROMPTED and REMINDED deadlines when the device acknowledges the command, or lengthen the demo windows to 15 s. Set the lease to at least 4× the heartbeat interval. Call setInsecure() from the start and disclose it on the §9 slide (https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/master/libraries/NetworkClientSecure/README.md); do not spend time pinning a root certificate at 3 a.m.

problems.problem: HMAC with a staleness check on X-Ts needs a synced clock. The ESP32 has no battery-backed clock: time is set through SNTP/settimeofday, and a power-on reset clears the RTC timer (https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/api-reference/system/system_time.html). After the lost-contact unplug and replug, every request is rejected as stale until NTP succeeds over the hotspot, so 'Contact restored' never appears.
problems.fix: Cut HMAC now. Use a static per-device bearer key header plus server-side dedupe on event_id. If you keep a timestamp, derive it from server_time in the last heartbeat reply, and key last_seq by boot_id so a reboot does not cause rejections.

problems.problem: Too many network dependencies, and the URL is unstable. cloudflared needs outbound TCP/UDP 7844 (https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/). Tiger Cloud uses a per-service high port, for example 30133 (https://docs.tigerdata.com/use-timescale/latest/services/connection-pooling), which campus Wi-Fi may block. Quick tunnels have 'no uptime guarantee' and 'the hostname changes each time' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/), so the printed QR card and the ESP32 URL break whenever cloudflared restarts, including if the laptop sleeps between submission and judging.

Consider Tailscale Funnel instead: it is free on all plans and gives a *.ts.net hostname on ports 443/8443/10000 (https://tailscale.com/kb/1223/funnel); confirm the hostname stays the same across restarts before relying on it. problems.problem: The kill -9 command can kill its own restart loop, and the server may not start at all on Windows. `pkill -f` matches the full command line (https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/pkill.1.html), so if the loop runs as `bash -c 'while true; do uvicorn …'`, the loop dies too and the server never returns on stage. On Windows, single-process uvicorn uses ProactorEventLoop (https://uvicorn.dev/concepts/event-loop/), which psycopg async does not support (https://www.psycopg.org/psycopg3/docs/advanced/async.html).
problems.fix: Run the loop from a script file whose name does not contain 'uvicorn', and kill by port: kill -9 $(lsof -ti tcp:8000). On Windows, start the server from run.py after asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy()), or run the backend on macOS or WSL. Rehearse the kill at G5.

The 4:00 slot holds a 30 s pitch, 7 scenarios, kill -9 and the judge joining, with about 40 s of pure countdown waiting in the 1:25–2:30 block. problems.problem: The head-drop 'fast drop' trigger cannot fire as specified. It measures angular rate only during quasi-static samples, but a 50°/s drop is by definition not quasi-static, so the trigger either never fires or fires at random.
problems.fix: Use one demo trigger: the angle from g_ref is at least θ_drop, held for at least 5 s, with SD(svm) below 0.05 g. Approximate the drop rate as the angle change between the last quasi-static sample before the drop and the first one after it, at most 1 s apart. Calibrate θ_phone on stage in 10 s.

problems.problem: Plan B pin mapping does not fit the Base Shield. The shield's Grove digital ports cover only D2–D8 (https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/Base_Shield_V2), so LEDs on D9 and D10 cannot be reached through Grove. JSON at 100 Hz over 115200 baud also uses most of the serial link.
problems.fix: Put Grove LED Sockets on ports D4, D6 and D8, the touch sensor on D2, and the FSR dividers on the A0 port (A0/A1) through a cut Grove cable. Stream compact CSV at 50 Hz, or raise the baud rate to 250000. Unplugging USB is the lost-contact demo.

problems.problem: The countdown can stall after a network blip. If the connection drops mid-transaction for a reason other than kill -9, the timer rows it holds with FOR UPDATE stay locked until Postgres notices. SKIP LOCKED then skips those timers, and escalation stalls.
problems.fix: Run ALTER ROLE tsdbadmin SET idle_in_transaction_session_timeout='10s' (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-client.html). Add keepalives=1&keepalives_idle=10 to DATABASE_URL, and give the Telegram poller its own dedicated connection for the advisory lock.

problems.problem: The append-only audit log blocks 'Delete my data'. A BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger plus REVOKE prevents user erasure unless there is an owner-role bypass, and the time is better spent elsewhere.
problems.fix: Keep the per-session sha256 hash chain. Drop REVOKE and the role split. Make the trigger allow DELETE only when SET LOCAL stillhere.erase='on' is set in the same transaction that writes the tombstone row.

problems.problem: The ESP32 NimBLE heart-rate client is risky and adds nothing. It would also compete for heap with TLS, while the laptop already reads heart rate.
problems.fix: Remove it from the plan entirely, and mention it only as roadmap.

## 1. Product summary and 30-second pitch

**StillHere** is a scrunchie that works as a hands-free safety check-in device. It is built for hair mode (worn in a ponytail) for nights with no pockets and no free hands. The same scrunchie also works on the wrist, using squeezes and LEDs only.

**How it works:**
- **Check-ins.**
  - Your Apple Watch taps you with a neutral message from a bot named "Reminders".
  - For a routine check-in, squeeze twice to answer "I'm OK".
  - The bot replies "Noted ✓" and the watch taps again.
- **Silent duress.**
  - Three short squeezes and then a 2-second hold, or the duress PIN, looks exactly like an "OK" or a cancel.
  - The watch shows the same "Noted ✓", but your contacts are silently asked for help.
- **Sensors only bring the next check-in forward.**
  - In the hair, an accelerometer notices a sustained change in head position. Your own Apple Watch supplies heart rate.
  - Neither decides that you are in trouble. An unusual change only makes StillHere ask sooner.
  - That early check-in needs a **counted** reply ("Reminder 3" means squeeze three times), so a reflex double squeeze cannot dismiss it.
- **Escalation happens only when you don't answer.**
  - A countdown in the database keeps running if your phone dies, or if we kill our own server live.
  - It alerts trusted contacts in order. Tapping "I'm on it" is not the end: that contact must confirm "I'm with her / she's safe", or the alert moves to the next person.
  - If nobody responds, a final step shows **"Emergency services: SIMULATED"**. No call is ever placed.
- **Lost contact is a separate alert,** with neutral wording.
- **Privacy and autonomy.**
  - Only contacts you approve are on the list, and contacts see nothing until an alert.
  - Your last-known location is released only at alert time, with its age shown, and the link expires.
  - Raw signals are deleted after 48 h.
- **Personal timeline.**
  - A hash-chained, timestamped record that you own and can export. Edits made after you export it are detectable.
  - It can help someone who cannot remember the night report it and ask for testing quickly.
  - There is no rapid drug screen for GHB-like drugs, and GHB becomes undetectable in blood within 4–8 h and in urine after at most 12 h ([Liechti & Kupferschmidt, Swiss Med Wkly 2004](https://smw.ch/index.php/smw/article/download/409/406/806)).

**30-second pitch.** Galit delivers it. It is about 60 words, which takes about 27 s at 140 wpm.

> "As of 2018, Statistics Canada filed drink spiking under 'other assaults' ([Global News](https://globalnews.ca/news/4367269/n-s-police-to-review-drink-tampering/amp)). The danger is the gap between when you can't ask for help and when anyone notices. In spy movies they hide weapons in their hair. We hide help in yours. Squeeze to check in. Sensors never decide; they only ask sooner. Don't answer, and your people are alerted until someone takes responsibility. Judge: you're Contact #2."

**Data flow:**
1. **Device to server.**
   - The scrunchie samples at 100 Hz and decodes squeezes and head position on the device.
   - Over USB serial it prints a heartbeat line every 1 s and event lines immediately.
   - `bridge.py` POSTs `/v1/device/heartbeat` every 2 s (demo), but only while device lines are arriving. It POSTs `/v1/device/events` immediately.
   - The heartbeat reply carries the downlink (`led`, `blink_n`, `challenge_id`), which `bridge.py` writes back over serial.
   - The device and heart-rate paths use `localhost`. The public URL is only for phones.
2. **Heart rate to server.**
   - The Apple Watch runs a HeartCast workout. The iPhone re-advertises heart rate as a standard BLE Heart Rate sensor.
   - The `/hr-bridge` page in Chrome subscribes to it and POSTs `/v1/hr` inside each notification handler, about once a second.
3. **Rules.** Every detector and the heart-rate rule can output only **`PULL_FORWARD`** (ARMED → PROMPTED with a counted challenge). Only a deadline expiring with no qualifying human response can reach `ESCALATED_*`.
4. **Side effects.**
   - Transitions write outbox rows.
   - `outbox_sender` delivers them to Telegram: contacts, and the wearer's "Reminders" chat, which reaches the watch.
   - `/c/<token>` polls `/v1/contact/<token>/status` every second.
5. **Acknowledgement.**
   - "I'm on it" moves the alert to ACKED, and the other contacts get "<name> is handling it".
   - Only "I'm with her / she's safe" or the wearer's real PIN closes the alert.

**Why this topology:**
- **USB serial is the default.** It removes the iPhone hotspot, crowded 2.4 GHz and the tunnel from the device path. Pulling the cable is the lost-contact demo.
- **Quick tunnels:**
  - They need no account. WebSockets work through them; SSE does not. They allow 200 in-flight requests ([Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/)).
  - They have "no uptime guarantee", and the hostname changes on every restart (same page).
  - They need outbound port 7844 ([Cloudflare firewall](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/)). If UDP is blocked, use `--protocol http2` ([run parameters](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/run-parameters/)).
- **Alternative: Tailscale Funnel.**
  - It is available on all plans (in beta). It listens only on 443, 8443 or 10000, and uses `*.ts.net` names in your tailnet's domain ([Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/kb/1223/funnel)).
  - Confirm at 18:45 that its hostname stays the same across restarts before relying on it.
- **ngrok's free tier is ruled out.** It adds an interstitial page and has a 20k requests/month cap ([ngrok](https://ngrok.com/docs/pricing-limits/free-plan-limits)).
- **Telegram long polling** (`getUpdates`) needs no public URL ([Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api)).
